taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes Dubois et al. (2021) place it in its own genus Boreorana; NatureServe keeps Lithobates sylvaticus.
fieldMarks: Dark mask running from each eye over the tympanum to the forelimb, with a white line along the upper lip.
Dorsolateral folds; webbed hind toes; smooth skin; a light mid-dorsal stripe may or may not be present; up to about 83 mm.
Colour ranges brown, tan, rust to green or grey; females larger; males have swollen thumb bases.
Call: rapid series of 1-8 (usually 3-5) rough clacking notes, like softly quacking ducks.
behavior: Winters on land and can freeze and thaw without harm.
Migrates to fish-free breeding pools in late winter or early spring and shows strong pond fidelity; mostly solitary otherwise.
Mostly diurnal, though breeding can occur at night; most active in summer in damp conditions.
Eats terrestrial invertebrates such as spiders, beetles, moth larvae, slugs and snails.
habitat: Wooded habitats including pond and stream edges, willow thickets and bogs; shelters in logs, humus and leaf litter; breeds in vernal pools and other fish-free ponds.
range: Northern Alaska across boreal Canada to Labrador and south to New Jersey, northern Georgia and northern Idaho, with spotty distribution south to northern Colorado and disjunct populations in Arkansas-Missouri; extends farther north than any other North American amphibian.
